<!--
SUPERSEDED. Kept for reference only -- this file is not part of the rebuilt
project and is known to be incorrect in several places. Do not source or knit
this for anything other than reading it against the replacement.

Known defects, each with a named regression test in tests/testthat/:

1. The "HW Model" chunk uses a constant `theta <- 0.05` inside the Euler loop.
   That is Vasicek with a constant long-run mean, not Hull-White -- the whole
   point of Hull-White is a time-dependent theta(t) fitted to today's curve,
   which this never does. Fixed by simulate_hull_white()'s theta(t)
   construction in R/short_rate.R, pinned by
   test_hull_white_reproduces_the_input_discount_curve_exactly_at_t_0 in
   tests/testthat/test-bond-prices.R.
2. The "CIR Model" chunk clips negative simulated rates to zero after every
   step (`short_rate[i] <- max(short_rate[i], 0)`). That is a reflecting
   barrier, not the CIR process: it injects extra probability mass just above
   zero on every step that would have gone negative, biasing the simulated
   mean upward. Fixed by simulate_cir()'s exact noncentral chi-square scheme
   (default) and documented full-truncation alternative in R/short_rate.R,
   pinned by the CIR moment and positivity tests in
   tests/testthat/test-short-rate.R.
3. `n <- T/dt` is used directly as a loop bound with no check that it is an
   integer number of steps, and could silently truncate. Fixed by
   .check_sim_inputs()'s integer step-count validation in R/short_rate.R,
   pinned by
   test_simulate_vasicek_rejects_a_horizon_that_is_not_an_integer_number_of_steps.
4. `T <- 1` shadows base R's `T`, the built-in alias for `TRUE` -- any later
   bare `T` in the same scope silently means 1, not true/false. Renamed to
   `Tt` throughout R/.
5. Every model chunk only ever plots one simulated path at one fixed seed, so
   nothing here characterizes a distribution, and there are no closed-form
   bond prices to check the simulation against at all. Fixed by vectorised
   many-path simulate_*() in R/short_rate.R and closed-form
   vasicek_bond_price(), cir_bond_price(), hull_white_bond_price() in
   R/bond_prices.R, cross-checked against Monte Carlo via mc_bond_price() and
   pinned by the "...bond price matches the closed form within 3 standard
   errors" tests in tests/testthat/test-bond-prices.R.
6. Nelson-Siegel is fit to 6 hardcoded maturity/yield points, with no test
   that the fit recovers known parameters or works on real data. Fixed by
   fit_ns() in R/nelson_siegel.R, pinned by
   test_fit_ns_recovers_known_parameters_from_synthetic_noiseless_data and
   test_fit_ns_has_small_rmse_on_the_cached_fred_curve in
   tests/testthat/test-nelson-siegel.R, with the curve itself coming from
   R/data.R.
7. `library(quantmod)`, `library(vars)` and `library(ggplot2)` are loaded and
   never used anywhere in the file. quantmod now does real work in R/data.R,
   ggplot2 produces the validation figures in R/validate.R, and vars is
   dropped -- there was never a VAR model here.

The working implementation is R/short_rate.R, R/bond_prices.R,
R/nelson_siegel.R and R/data.R, run through run.R and documented in
docs/VALIDATION.md.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(stats)
library(minpack.lm)
library(quantmod)
library(vars)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}



models <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Vasicek", "CIR", "Hull-White", "Black-Karasinski", "Nelson-Siegel"),
  Uniqueness = c(
    "Mean-reverting with constant volatility.",
    "Non-negativity via square-root volatility.",
    "Time-dependent mean reversion.",
    "Logarithmic modeling of the short rate.",
    "Empirical yield curve representation."
  ),
  Pro = c(
    "Analytical tractability.",
    "Ensures positive rates.",
    "Fits initial yield curve.",
    "Ensures positive rates.",
    "Intuitive interpretation of parameters."
  ),
  Con = c(
    "Allows negative rates.",
    "Difficult to calibrate.",
    "Increased calibration complexity.",
    "Requires numerical solutions.",
    "Lacks arbitrage-free properties."
  )
)

kable(models, format = "latex", longtable = T, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Comparison of Interest Rate Models") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F) %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T) %>% 
  column_spec(2, width = "10em") %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "10em") %>%
  column_spec(4, width = "10em")

```

```{r Vasicek Model, echo=TRUE}
r0 <- 0.03
a <- 0.1
b <- 0.05
sigma <- 0.02
T <- 1
dt <- 1/252
n <- T/dt

short_rate <- numeric(n)
short_rate[1] <- r0


set.seed(123)


for (i in 2:n) {
  dW <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(dt))
  short_rate[i] <- short_rate[i-1] + a * (b-short_rate[i-1]) * dt + sigma * dW
}

plot(short_rate, 
     type = "l", 
     col = "blue", 
     xlab = "Time Step", 
     ylab = "Interest Rate", 
     main = "Vasicek Model")

```


```{r CIR Model, echo=TRUE}


a <- 0.1     
b <- 0.05    
sigma <- 0.02 
r0 <- 0.03   
T <- 1       
dt <- 1/252  
n <- T/dt    

# short rate
short_rate <- numeric(n)
short_rate[1] <- r0

set.seed(123)
for (i in 2:n) {
  dW <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(dt))
  short_rate[i] <- short_rate[i-1] + a * (b - short_rate[i-1]) * dt + sigma * sqrt(short_rate[i-1]) * dW
  short_rate[i] <- max(short_rate[i], 0)  # Ensure non-negativity
}


plot(short_rate, type = "l", col = "darkgreen", xlab = "Time Step", ylab = "Interest Rate", main = "CIR Model Simulation")
```


```{r HW Model, echo = TRUE}


a <- 0.1     
sigma <- 0.02
r0 <- 0.03   
T <- 1       
dt <- 1/252  
n <- T/dt    
short_rate <- numeric(n)
short_rate[1] <- r0


set.seed(123)
for (i in 2:n) {
  dW <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(dt))
  theta <- 0.05
  short_rate[i] <- short_rate[i-1] + a * (theta - short_rate[i-1]) * dt + sigma * dW
}

plot(short_rate, type = "l", col = "blue", xlab = "Time Step", ylab = "Interest Rate", main = "Hull-White Model Simulation")
```




```{r Black - Karasinski Model}

a <- 0.1     
sigma <- 0.02 
r0 <- 0.03   
T <- 1       
dt <- 1/252  
n <- T/dt    


short_rate <- numeric(n)
short_rate[1] <- log(r0)


set.seed(123)
for (i in 2:n) {
  dW <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(dt))
  short_rate[i] <- short_rate[i-1] + a * (log(0.05) - short_rate[i-1]) * dt + sigma * dW
}


short_rate <- exp(short_rate)


plot(short_rate, type = "l", col = "brown", xlab = "Time Step", ylab = "Interest Rate", main = "Black-Karasinski Model Simulation")

```

```{r Nelson-Sigel}

library(minpack.lm)


nelson_siegel <- function(t, beta0, beta1, beta2, lambda) {
  return(beta0 + beta1 * (1 - exp(-lambda * t)) / (lambda * t) + beta2 * ((1 - exp(-lambda * t)) / (lambda * t) - exp(-lambda * t)))
}


maturity <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10)
yield <- c(0.02, 0.025, 0.027, 0.03, 0.032, 0.035)


ns_model <- nlsLM(yield ~ nelson_siegel(maturity, beta0, beta1, beta2, lambda),
                  start = list(beta0 = 0.03, beta1 = -0.01, beta2 = 0.01, lambda = 0.5))

summary(ns_model)


fitted_yield <- predict(ns_model)
plot(maturity, yield, pch = 19, col = "red", xlab = "Maturity (Years)", ylab = "Yield", main = "Nelson-Siegel Yield Curve")
lines(maturity, fitted_yield, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

```
